briefing.full.hot: Top-level layout of the daily briefing email/dashboard text. Sections are named params ({title} {tldr} {body} {leaving} {fresh_air} {grace} {steps} {tonight} {suggestions}); you may reorder or drop sections. Keep the 40-character rule lines and the blank lines between sections. Same for warm/mild/cool/cold/other.
briefing.tldr: The short push-notification text (Android/iOS cap ~255 chars shown). Rows are whole messages; keep one row per line.
briefing.band: A temperature range: {lo} is a bare number, {hi} carries the unit symbol (e.g. 68–74°F). Keep the en dash; do not add a second unit symbol.
briefing.close_when: 'now' when the windows should already be closed, otherwise a clock time. Used inside other sentences (e.g. 'Close by now' / 'Close by 11:00 AM').
briefing.reason.comfort_floor: A clause inside 'Close up {when} {reason}.' - why the windows close. Lower case, no final period.
briefing.reason.outdoor_rise: A clause inside 'Close up {when} {reason}.' - why the windows close. Lower case, no final period.
briefing.reason.trap_warmth: A clause inside 'Close up by {time} {reason}.' Lower case, no final period.
briefing.hot.plan: Paragraph slots of the hot-day plan; each is a whole paragraph message. Placement and separators are yours.
briefing.hot.blinds_after_close: {evening} is yes/no: 'yes' ends the sentence after the temperature (another paragraph follows about reopening); 'no' adds 'for the rest of the day'.
briefing.warm.ac_breach: {windows} yes/no: whether windows are being advised today (adds 'Once windows are closed, ...').
briefing.reopen_evening: {ac_off} yes/no: 'yes' adds the promise that the AC will be turned off. {time} is a clock time.
briefing.leaving.home_cool: {minutes} is a count of minutes (plural). Wording about 'drift up' = the house is allowed to get warmer while nobody is home.
briefing.fresh.cool: {minutes} is the delay (plural) before the AC pauses for an open window. {away} yes/no: 'yes' omits the sentence about pulling back down to {target}.
briefing.fresh.heat: {minutes} is the delay (plural) before the heat pauses for an open window.
briefing.fresh.other: {away} yes/no: 'yes' omits the dash clause with the band.
briefing.grace.manual: 'N minutes hands-off window': a period in which door/window sensors do not pause the HVAC. English reads 'a 5 minutes hands-off window'; use correct grammar for your language.
briefing.grace.automation: 'N minutes settling period' after the system resumed the HVAC.
briefing.steps: Heading plus a rule line, then the list of today's steps (each already a '  • ...' line) - {now} is an optional first line.
briefing.suggestions: Heading plus a rule line, then bullet lines ({items}), then the closing instruction about the dashboard AI tab.
briefing.tonight.plan: {adaptive} is an optional extra line directly under {first}.
